flawed_step: The claim that every max-degree greedy execution returns a minimum vertex cover; picking a maximum-degree vertex, with ties broken arbitrarily, need not belong to any minimum cover.
counterexample: Path P5: a-b-c-d-e (edges ab, bc, cd, de). The minimum vertex cover is {b,d}, size 2. Greedy run: the degrees are a1,b2,c2,d2,e1, so pick c (max degree 2), which deletes bc and cd. The remaining edges ab and de have max degree 1: pick a, which deletes ab, then pick d, which deletes de. The output is {c,a,d}, size 3 > 2.
assessment_summary: On P5, choosing the center vertex c (a legal tie-break at max degree 2) forces two more picks, giving a cover of size 3, while {b,d} is a cover of size 2. The statement is false.
